question: A library shelf started with 34 books in the morning. By midday, 16 were checked out by students. Then 63 books were returned by patrons. During the afternoon, 17 books were sent to be repaired. By evening, donations added 20 new books. The librarian doubled the shelf count to prepare for the week. Finally, 69 more books arrived from the warehouse. How many books were on the shelf at the end of the day?

A soccer team had 103 training passes to work with. They multiplied passes by 9 for advanced drills. They then tripled that set for 7 different practice sessions. The coach added 11 cones to mark zones. He then multiplied the zones by 9 for expansion. Finally, 21 additional cones arrived for setup. The field had cost 500 dollars to prepare. How many training resources did the team have?

A gardener planted 59 tomato seeds initially. He multiplied his planting by 9 to expand the garden. He doubled the rows for better organization. He then added 73 saplings he'd grown elsewhere. He removed 47 damaged seedlings from the garden. David had helped plant 30 seedlings last season. How many healthy plants did the gardener have?

A bank account started with 168 dollars. A withdrawal of 105 was made for expenses. The remaining balance was then multiplied by 4 through an investment. Then 47 dollars in interest was added. That sum was multiplied by 5 for monthly compounding. The entire amount was multiplied by 8 for quarterly calculations. The customer had deposited money 6 times last year. What was the final account balance?

A shop sold 208 items in the first week. It sold 205 items the second week. They added 6 items to inventory. Then added 20 more items. They added 28 items from a new shipment. Converting to dozen lots showed the final count. The store manager worked 8 days that month. How many items did the shop have total?

A factory produced 185 units Monday. They multiplied production by 8 for the Tuesday shift. They multiplied again by 8 for Wednesday. They added 45 units from returns. They subtracted 3481 defective units. The remainder was multiplied by 6 for new packaging. Then 25 bonus units were added. A different factory made 60 units. How many final units did this factory have?

A student started with 60 marbles. She removed 40 during a game with friends. She gained 53 marbles from winning trades. She multiplied her collection by 8 through careful organization. She then split them equally in half with her brother. Marcus had 30 marbles of his own. How many marbles did the student end up with?

A collector had 116 coins on Monday. He tripled his collection through purchases. He added 42 rare coins on Wednesday. He added 29 more coins from an auction. He added 61 vintage coins to complete a set. He had given away 25 coins to a friend last month. How many coins did the collector have in total?

A restaurant served 232 meals on opening day. They removed 133 from the counter for catering. They multiplied the remaining meals by 3 for weekend prep. They multiplied by 2 for holiday events. They added 68 meals from new menu items. They added 71 pre-ordered meals to the kitchen. They had planned to serve 500 customers this month. How many total meals were prepared?

A coach had 97 basketballs initially. He multiplied the supply by 4 through donations. He removed 278 old balls for recycling. He added 75 new balls from inventory. He doubled the final count for tournament preparation. The gym budget was 2000 dollars. How many basketballs did the coach have ready?

A farmer started with 152 apple trees. He added 23 new saplings to his orchard. He multiplied the rows by 7 for organization. He multiplied by 2 for split shifting work. He multiplied by 8 for seasonal expansion plans. He owned 5 other orchards across town. How many apple trees did the farmer manage in this location?

A store started with 76 toys in inventory. They multiplied stock by 9 for restocking. They added 64 toys from a supplier delivery. They added 35 more toys in the evening. They added 22 toys from returns. They removed 622 toy units for a recall. The store manager worked 40 hours a week. How many toys remained on the shelves?

A publisher had 194 books printed. They added 13 copies for author events. They multiplied the total by 5 for book club orders. They removed 21 damaged copies. They multiplied by 6 for regional distribution. They removed 745 books for clearance sales. The print run cost 3000 dollars. How many books did the publisher have left?

A museum had 75 artifacts on display initially. They added 77 new pieces to a collection. They removed 25 for conservation cleaning. They removed 99 more pieces temporarily. They added back 65 restored pieces. The facility opened to the public 6 days a week. How many artifacts were on display at the end?

A trainer had 112 hours of classes scheduled. He doubled the schedule for expansion. He added 75 new student hours to the calendar. He doubled again for summer camps. He multiplied by 7 for weekend workshops. He added 52 hours from evening sessions. He added 61 emergency tutoring hours. The gym charged 25 dollars per hour. How many total training hours did he schedule?

A charity had 64 boxes of supplies to distribute. They split the boxes equally among 4 communities. They again split equally among 4 homes per community. They multiplied by 7 to account for family sizes. They multiplied by 3 for donation drives. They added 19 emergency boxes. They had 100 volunteers. How many supply boxes were distributed?

A hotel had 140 rooms initially. They added 16 new suites from expansion. They divided rooms equally among 4 floors for management. Each floor multiplied its allocation by 7. They subtracted 253 rooms for maintenance. They added 39 newly renovated rooms. They had 200 employees total. How many rooms were available to rent?

A coach had 77 baseballs to work with. He added 20 more for practice. He multiplied the supply by 7 times. He removed 648 old balls from storage. He multiplied the remaining by 4 for league play. The team had 25 players total. How many baseballs did the coach have ready?

A factory started with 57 units on Monday. They multiplied by 4 through morning production. They multiplied by 8 for afternoon shifts. They multiplied by 2 for quality control batches. They multiplied by 8 for the weekly total. They divided by 2 for split distribution. The facility employed 40 workers. How many final units were produced?

A farm had 181 eggs collected by morning. They added 69 more from afternoon collection. They divided the total equally by 5 for packaging. They added 41 eggs from evening laying. They removed 14 eggs that cracked. The farm had 8 chickens producing eggs. How many eggs were ready for sale?

A store started with 82 items on the shelf Monday. They multiplied by 8 through afternoon stocking. They multiplied by 2 for evening expansion. They multiplied by 3 for comprehensive inventory. They divided by 3 for quality sorting. The manager worked 8-hour shifts. How many items passed quality check?

A factory produced 210 units initially. They multiplied by 8 for a large order. They added 79 bonus units. They multiplied by 5 for packaging lots. They added 67 units from another line. They added 13 more for shipment padding. The facility opened 6 days a week. How many total units were shipped?

A warehouse had 150 boxes Monday morning. They multiplied by 3 through the day. They multiplied by 2 for shipment organization. They added 58 boxes from a delivery. They removed 184 boxes for store distribution. The building was 5000 square feet. How many boxes remained?

A farm started with 84 apples initially. They multiplied by 5 through harvest. They added 23 apples from a neighbor. They multiplied by 6 for packing. They added 78 apples from a second harvest. They removed 1963 apples for cider production. They multiplied the remainder by 8 for market sale. The orchard had 20 trees. How many apples went to market?

A student had 177 coins initially. They multiplied by 3 through pocket money. They removed 529 coins for a purchase. They added 74 coins from a gift. They added 6 more coins found. His brother had 30 coins too. How many coins did the student have?
